title: M. africanum as a human-adapted name
dek: West-African lineages L5/L6 sit inside MTBC. Wikipedia's species page is a geography-and-membership card, not a different DST catalogue.
story: M. africanum is Wikipedia's name for human-adapted MTBC that is not M. tuberculosis sensu stricto — currently discussed as lineages L5 and L6 (with rarer African lineages nearby). It is TB, it is MTBC, and it is geographically concentrated in West Africa.
Laboratories outside that geography still see it in travellers and in mixed reference collections. The failure mode is forcing every MTBC genome into an L4 prior.
RD9 is deleted relative to Mtb sensu stricto — the same deletion class as animal-adapted members — which is why a naive RD panel can confuse africanum with bovis if you stop at one marker.
deepTitle: Lineage as covariate, not as drug
deep: Do not invent a different first-line backbone because the Wikipedia lead says 'africanum'. WHO treatment of DS-TB does not fork on this name.
Mutation-rate and PE/PPE differences are covariates for a GWAS or a catalogue prior, the same warning as on the Beijing plate.
L9 and other rare African lineages are sampling updates; membership lists lag.
Speciation reports should say africanum/L5/L6 explicitly when the barcode supports it.

visual.caption: Teaching bars: geographic concentration and RD9 status versus Mtb sensu stricto. Not a prevalence survey.

example.title: One-marker RD9 panic
example.setup: RD9 PCR negative. Someone files the isolate as M. bovis and strips PZA from a pulmonary DS-TB regimen before SNP barcode.

steps.title: RD9 is a clade, not a species
steps.body: Africanum and animal-adapted MTBC both lose RD9.

steps.title: Add RD1 and SNPs
steps.body: RD1 present plus africanum SNPs is not bovis.

steps.title: Treatment fork is DST, not the English name
steps.body: DS africanum is still a DS-TB problem once PZA is actually tested/genotyped.

example.takeaway: Africanum is human-adapted MTBC with an RD9 trap.

check.prompt: M. africanum pulmonary disease that is RIF-S on Ultra is best treated as:
choices: TB disease inside MTBC; regimen from WHO DS/DR rules, not from the species epithet
check.answer: TB disease inside MTBC; regimen from WHO DS/DR rules, not from the species epithet
check.why: The name is geography and lineage, not a fourth-line drug.

whyWrong.Automatic BPaLM: That is a DR-TB regimen class.

check.prompt: RD9 deleted, RD1 present, SNP barcode L5. This is:
check.why: RD1-present excludes BCG; L5 is africanum.

check.prompt: On the small-multiples plate, what are the 'still TB disease' bars teaching?
choices: That africanum is twice as pathogenic
That both names are disease-capable MTBC, not a severity score
That West Africa has no Mtb sensu stricto
check.answer: That both names are disease-capable MTBC, not a severity score

whyWrong.That West Africa has no Mtb sensu strict: Panel one is a prior, not a zero.
